blocks.content: As you've learned three types of storage in the previous chapter, you can use any of them to store the player scores.
Since we want the scores to persist even after the page is reloaded, we'll use local storage.

Here, saveScores() checks if the player already has a score stored in the localStorage. If it exists, it updates as necessary. Else, it creates an empty list and adds a new entry to it containing the names and scores of both players.
With this, you've completed your first browser-based game using JS.
